title: remaining gaps in US_STATES
headline: US_STATES needs no dictionary expansion. Exhaustive scans of the six-file US address token union (4510 distinct tokens) find zero unhandled state spellings, zero unhandled two-letter state codes, and zero misspellings. One small real exception: 'del' is unhandled (D074 wrongly claimed it resolves), plus the already-known 'penn'.

arithmetic.france_rows_derivation: 0 + 0 + 0 + 259452 + 703378 + 731615 = 1694445 (France absent from all three train files)
arithmetic.absence_bound: A token absent from all six top-4000 lists occurs fewer than 101 times in test_s1 and fewer than 201 in train_s1, i.e. under ~1681 summed across all six files. 'Absent' never means 'does not occur'.

source_quotes.selfmap_omits_fr_regions: The loop tuple is (US_STATES, IN_STATES) only; FR_REGIONS is absent, which is the separate D070/D073 defect and is not US_STATES' problem.
source_quotes.last_match_wins: _upstream/src/normalize.py:333-335 -> if ck in smap: state = smap[ck]; continue  (no break, so the last matching component overwrites)
source_quotes.flat_counter: build_profile.py:126-127 splits on [,;] and pushes [a-z0-9]+ matches into one flat Counter, discarding component boundaries
source_quotes.prune: build_profile.py:45-48 prune(c, keep_min=1) deletes count <= 1 tokens

new_findings.claim: 'del' is an unhandled token; D074's claim that it resolves is FALSE.
new_findings.evidence: del in_literal=False, in_runtime104=False. US_STATES holds 'delaware'->'de' (literal) and 'de'->'de' (self-map). 'del' is a different string from the code 'de'.

new_findings.claim: Exhaustive: none of the 33 two-character alphabetic US address tokens (4001717 occurrences) is a state abbreviation.

Exhaustive edit-distance<=1 scan: 6 non-key tokens (154515 occurrences) are within one edit of a state name, all ordinary English words (main, indian, fontana, mine, marine, marina). No misspelled state exists.
The self-map loop is load-bearing for US_STATES: 45 of 52 canonical codes appear as input tokens for 7354018 occurrences. Unlike FR_REGIONS, it has real effect here.

The Washington/DC collision is real: 'district of columbia'->dc and 'washington'->'wa' share the US bucket and last-match-wins has no positional guard. A DC row written '..., Washington, DC 20001' resolves to the wrong state wa. Exposure bounded above by dc occurrences, <=35681 rows (<=0.2976%), and that bound is loose.
new_findings.note: This is a normalize_address matcher defect, not a dictionary-content defect. No US_STATES entry would fix it.

new_findings.claim: Case sensitivity is a non-issue: normalize.py:317 lowercases all input and build_profile.py:110,113 lowercases before tokenising, so the profile cannot represent an uppercase token at all.

independently_confirmed: 52 literal entries, 52 distinct values, 104 runtime entries, 0 self-maps missing (D074)
50 states + dc + pr; 40 single-word + 12 multi-word keys (D074)
wy->way is the ONLY non-identity ADDR_CANON_COMMON collision among the 104 runtime keys; the four other hits mt, fl, ct, ne are identity (D074)
zero occurrences of hand-picked misspellings calif, fla, mass, tenn, wisc, minn, conn, colo, okla, ariz (D074 section 11, strengthened by NEW-3)
US_STATES unreachable from France and India rows (D074 section 3)

france_relevance.reason: France is the scored country and is absent from training (0 France rows in train_s1/2/3; 1694445 France rows all in test). US_STATES is country-keyed at normalize.py:318 and is unreachable from any France row, so no finding in this report can move the France score.
france_relevance.largest_overlaps_are_ordinary_french_wor: de=1050023, la=481231, which are not US states here
france_relevance.recommendation: Deprioritise this dictionary for the France objective; the France dictionaries hold the remaining value.

recommendations.action: Do NOT add states, territories or abbreviations to US_STATES.
Optionally add 'del'->'de' and 'penn'->'pa' (13795 occurrences, 0.115% of US rows).
Do NOT touch the self-maps; all 52 are present and load-bearing.
Fix the positional matcher instead (require a state match to be the final component or be followed only by a postcode). Highest-value US item, ahead of any dictionary edit.
Deprioritise US_STATES for the France objective.

gaps: All negatives are bounded by TOPN=4000 truncation, not absolute. Absence from the top 4000 is never proof of non-occurrence.
prune() deletes count<=1 tokens, so singletons are invisible system-wide and cannot be bounded at 1.

The 12 multi-word keys are structurally unmeasurable: TOKEN_RE=[a-z0-9]+ stores 'new york' as 'new' and 'york' separately and no bigram or component field exists. No claim is made about multi-word coverage.
No row-level counts: addr_tokens is a flat Counter with component boundaries discarded, so every figure is a token occurrence or an explicitly labelled upper bound on rows.
Cannot confirm del/penn appear as standalone state components rather than inside street names, so the fix is LIKELY not CONFIRMED.
Did not re-derive the France pin guard or the FR_REGIONS resolution rate, per the work order.
bottom_line: This dictionary is fine for this dataset; the remaining defect is theoretical only, with one small real exception ('del', plus the already-known 'penn'). Every state token the data contains is already a canonical key. The only live US defect is in normalize_address's positional logic, not in the dictionary.
